subject: Post-call: Deployment mode & migration follow-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Deployment mode & migration follow-ups

Thanks again for the time today, Jacob — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Call highlights:
- Current setup: using OpenAI API for most production traffic and a legacy on-prem A100 cluster for experimental models.
- Primary needs: predictable throughput for customer-facing inference, stricter data controls for PHI-ish telemetry, and a migration path that minimizes downtime for our real-time endpoints.

Deployment mode considerations (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, lowest friction for evals/proofs-of-concept; recommended for initial model parity checks and small-scale UAT.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable p99 latency and throughput; recommended if you need sustained throughput and SLA-backed behavior without managing infra.
- Private VPC / on-prem: best when you need full network isolation or strict data residency/compliance (we support customer-managed VPCs and an on-prem package in special cases).

Migration path suggestion (from today’s chat):
1) Start with Hosted API for parity testing and to run your evals against representative traffic.
2) Move to Dedicated for production if you need predictable capacity; we can size a reserved pool based on your peak QPS and sequence lengths.
3) If regulatory or residency requirements mandate it, we can plan a Private VPC/on-prem deployment but that typically adds integration/backfill work (KMS, audit logs, network peering).

Immediate next steps:
- Attached a draft mutual action plan that lays out milestones for evaluation -> pilot -> production (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx).
- Can Dev (cc’d) run a technical deep-dive next week to review SSO, network requirements, and model compatibility.
- Quick ask: could you confirm (a) expected peak requests/sec, (b) average and 95th-percentile sequence length, and (c) any hard compliance blockers we should know about?

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue 5/11 10am PT, Tue 5/11 3pm PT, Wed 5/12 10am PT. Let me know which works and we’ll lock in.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing the momentum.

—

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: Deployment mode & migration follow-ups — technical notes

Hi Jacob — thanks for the diagram and the details. Quick technical notes and a recommended phased approach: 

Phase 0 — Parity/Eval (Hosted API):
- Use Hosted API to run your parity tests against the same model versions and prompt sets. This avoids early infra work and lets you validate quality metrics.
- We support streaming/responses and function-style tool-calling so we can mirror your current API flow.

Phase 1 — Pilot (Dedicated):
- Dedicated pools reserve GPUs for you; we’ll size based on sustained tokens/sec and peak r/s. For your ~25 r/s with avg 600 tokens, we’d estimate an initial 2 x A100-style equivalents or a multi-node M-class pool (we’ll refine sizing after telemetry).
- KV/cache: we support prefix/KV caching and can import cache warmup strategies; you’ll want to plan cache priming during cutover.
- Model artifacts: model checkpoints can be loaded if they are in compatible formats (PyTorch/Transformers); we’ll run a conversion/validation step.

Phase 2 — Production & Migration:
- Rolling cutover using traffic-weighted routing and canary policies to validate latency and quality.
- If you need VPC peering for Dedicated, we can configure secure networking and private egress (ask infra team for allowlist ranges).

Compliance & SSO:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; I’ve attached a pointer to the checklist and a redacted evidence pack we can share under an NDA (SOC2-type2-redwood-evidence.pdf).
- SSO: we support Azure AD SAML/OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning — we’ll send a short integration guide.

Attachments: TECHNICAL_DEEPDIVE.pdf (slide stub), SOC2-type2-redwood-evidence.pdf (redacted evidence stub)

A few asks to help us size and plan the pilot: 
- Sample prompt set or a small eval harness (10–50 typical queries)
- Expected RPS during business hours vs off-hours
- Any hard cutoff for migration downtime or SLA windows that procurement requires

Happy to walk through this Wed 5/12 10am PT — I’ll include a short agenda: network/SSO, sizing, cache strategy, artifact validation.

Best,
Dev Patel
